title: Projection and quotient-unit normalization of strict-limit reindexing
statement: For d,A,T,T prime,u as in lem-pur-completed-module-section-reindexing, let P be the ordinary completed-ring pullback and H its strict termwise action. There is an isomorphism beta: lim_T followed by P -> H followed by lim_Tprime whose component composed with every target projection equals P of the source projection. There is an isomorphism b: Rlim_T followed by d.pull u -> d.towerPull u followed by Rlim_Tprime. On a K-injective strict tower complex I it satisfies the comparison-unit equation: Pderived(eta_lim(I)); b(QI); Rlim_Tprime(factor_H(I)) equals factor_P(lim I); Q(beta_I); eta_lim(HI). For every derived K, ordinaryToCompleted(u,K) equals d.pull u applied to completionUnit(K), followed by b on the strict reduction tower of K. No completeness hypothesis is imposed here; invertibility of the completion unit is not asserted. The coefficient datum and the concrete canonical maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and [def-pur-completed-reindexing-data].

proof.text: The ordinary module equivalence and its strict termwise equivalence have exact reverse functors as left adjoints. Apply the exact-adjoint tower model construction (using a small model of the site when needed) and the strict derived-limit computation. The ordinary comparison is uniquely fixed by the projections; its image on K-injective resolutions defines the derived comparison and its inverse. The derived-pair unit formula is precisely the displayed equation.

On a constant tower, the ordinary limit comparison carries the constant-tower unit to the target constant-tower unit: at a tower resolution the two maps factor the identical compatible family of reindexed component maps through the target limit. Projection uniqueness proves their equality. Apply naturality of b to the strict quotient augmentation. By the definition of ordinaryToCompleted as constant-tower unit followed by the pulled augmentation, the resulting equality is the last asserted equation.
